title: perf(canary): implement adaptive latency/throughput autodetect + rollout guards
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: reduce noisy rollouts and catch subtle latency/throughput regressions early by making the perf-canary detector adaptive to workload shifts and KV cache dynamics, with stronger rollout guards. This PR implements an adaptive auto-detection algorithm that adjusts thresholds based on recent baseline distributions (sequence-length buckets, KV cache hit-rate) and adds hysteresis to prevent flapping. It also expands rollout guard policies to enforce minimum canary sample size, automatic rollback on sustained regressions, and traffic-shifting constraints when backend capacity is limited. The description below summarizes design, tests, and rollout plan. Design summary: 1) Adaptive detector: computes per-bucket baselines for p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput; baselines are maintained with an exponentially-weighted window and stratified by sequence-length and model variant. 2) Sensitivity profiles: three presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) + custom config; each maps to multipliers on stddev thresholds and min-sample requirements. 3) KV-aware adjustments: detector lowers sensitivity for requests hitting large KV cache ratios and tightens for cold-cache traffic. 4) Hysteresis: require sustained regression across N windows (configurable) before triggering rollback; allow a grace window for autoscaling events. 5) Rollout guards: enforce canary traffic floor/ceiling, require performance pass & health checks before traffic ramp, and automatic staged rollback with metadata annotated in rollout events. 6) Integrations: emits standardized perf_canary.alert events, ties to SRE-runbooks, and exposes tuning knobs in the console. Testing & validation: unit tests for detector logic, integration tests with synthetic traffic (varying seq-len, cache hit rates), canary smoke job run in CI, and a staged deployment to canary namespace for production verification. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated cluster for 24h with conservative sensitivity, monitor for p95 regressions > configured threshold, then gradual ramp. Checklist: - [x] core detection algorithm implementation - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] KV-aware heuristics - [x] rollout guard enforcement and API surface - [x] console/config surface + docs - [x] perf-canary CI smoke job - [x] runbook and SRE handoff Notes: tuned defaults to conservative after SRE review; sensitivity and hysteresis values live in perf-canary configs (see files changed). Related: ENG-4829, SRE-221, SUP-1298.

review_comments: Priya Natarajan: overall looks good — can you justify the default hysteresis=3 windows? worried about false positives during autoscaling.

Liam Chen: replied: hysteresis=3 chosen after running synthetic 72h traces; added grace window for autoscale events in detector to avoid penalizing transient scaling. Added tests that simulate scale spikes.
Marta Ruiz: request_changes: please add an e2e that includes cold-KV traffic (we've seen regressions that only show up in cold-cache).
Liam Chen: addressed: added integration test that exercises low KV hit-rate paths and updated docs to call out expected sensitivity differences. PTAL.
Omar Khouri: approved: smoke CI passed, unit/integration green, load test on canary cluster showed no regressions with conservative profile.
release_notes: Adds an adaptive performance canary detector that stratifies baselines by sequence length and KV cache hit-rate, plus rollout guards that enforce staged rollouts, minimum canary sample sizes, and automatic rollback on sustained regressions. Defaults use a conservative sensitivity profile. See docs/perf-canary.md for tuning.
notes: SRE to monitor first 24h after rollout; conservative profile recommended for initial fleets. Config path: perf-canary/config_defaults.yaml. If aggressive profile is enabled, ensure additional traffic capacity to avoid false positives due to autoscaling.
